stem: A nurse manager uses current research findings together with clinical expertise when developing a unit protocol. Which approach does this represent?

options.B: Practice based only on unit tradition
options.C: Research use that is separate from clinical decision-making
options.D: A protocol process that excludes clinical expertise

rationale: AHRQ defines evidence-based practice as healthcare guided by thoughtful integration of the best available scientific knowledge with clinical expertise. AHRQ also notes that evidence can be translated into practice-wide protocols. A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize evidence-based practice as integration of best available evidence with clinical expertise in care and protocol decisions.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_document_title: Evidence-Based Practice; Key Driver 1: Seek, Select, and Customize the Best Evidence for Use by the Practice
source_version_date: Current AHRQ topic page; implementation guidance accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Evidence-Based Practice definition; Key Driver 1 — translation of evidence into practice-wide protocols
source_claim_supported: Evidence-based practice integrates best available scientific knowledge with clinical expertise, and evidence can be translated/customized into practice protocols.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — evidence-based practice, quality improvement, and care standards
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — evidence-based protocol development

source_original.stem: A nurse manager encourages staff to review current nursing research literature when developing new unit protocols. This practice reflects the value of:

options.A: Use evidence-based practice only in academic settings and not when designing bedside protocols
options.B: Treat research as separate from clinical care because studies do not guide nursing interventions
options.C: Rely on unit tradition alone even when stronger current research supports a different approach
options.D: Integrate current research evidence with clinical expertise when developing nursing protocols

source_original.rationale: Incorporating current nursing research findings into clinical decision-making and protocol development reflects the value of evidence-based practice, helping ensure that nursing care and unit protocols are grounded in the most current, effective, and safe standards of care, rather than relying solely on tradition or personal experience.
source_original.source_detail: Evidence-based practice integrates current research evidence into clinical protocols and decisions; reviewed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Replaced a generic AACN homepage with current AHRQ evidence-based-practice definitions and protocol implementation guidance. Rebuilt the options so the correct answer is the named concept rather than a long definitional sentence; correct-option letter changed from D to A after correction.

audit_findings.currentness: AHRQ current evidence-based-practice topic page checked 2026-08-17; implementation guidance also reviewed.
audit_findings.claim_audit: AHRQ directly defines EBP as integration of scientific knowledge and clinical expertise and describes translating evidence into practice protocols.

distractor_audit.B: Tradition alone is not evidence-based practice.
distractor_audit.C: Research is intended to inform clinical decision-making.
distractor_audit.D: Clinical expertise is part of evidence-based practice, not excluded.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: A is the sole named approach matching the stem.
audit_findings.cueing: Correct answer is concise and distractors are competing practice approaches.
audit_findings.blueprint: Evidence use and protocol development fit Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked AHRQ EBP definition and protocol translation guidance; A remains uniquely correct.
